title: Separate native navigation target from current destination

scope.subject: Keep native YEIS travel and Locate destinations pending until autopilot completion so ACTIVE and aria-current=location never claim an unarrived or failed target

research_summary: UniverseNavigator currently renders activeDestinationId as ACTIVE and aria-current=location. UniverseApp assigns that id before native YEIS travel/Locate actually completes, so a failed route can still appear as the current location after the failure notice is dismissed. WAI-ARIA defines aria-current as the current item and the location token as the current location within an environment/context; selected/pending and current can intentionally differ. React likewise treats pending state as distinct feedback while the final state is not yet shown. Keep product System/Planet opens immediate because the rendered product scene changes immediately, but native camera requests must carry destinationId, publish a separate pending destination/mode while autopilot runs, promote it to active only in the existing completion callback, and clear pending on failure. This retains one YEIS navigation authority and one destination model.

sources.finding: WAI-ARIA defines aria-current as the element representing the current item; aria-current=location represents the current location. It explicitly distinguishes current from selected-next semantics.

React's transition guidance treats pending visual state as distinct from the final state that is shown after asynchronous work completes, supporting an explicit pending destination rather than optimistic ACTIVE.
Pinned MIT YEIS remains the native camera/navigation authority; its autopilot completion remains the correct point at which a native target becomes the current spatial destination.
Pinned MIT TourPlayer keeps flying distinct from arrived/dwell, reinforcing that commanded camera target and arrived location are separate states.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep YEIS autopilot and its arrival semantics as the native spatial authority; do not add another router or flight controller.
Existing React state is sufficient to represent current versus pending destination explicitly; useTransition itself is not required because native completion is already callback-driven.
Extend the existing native camera request metadata with destinationId and promote pending to active only through the existing completion callback.
Reuse aria-current exactly for arrived/current location and expose pending state visually without claiming aria-current.

candidates.name: Existing pinned YEIS native arrival callback
candidates.reason: Already determines when native camera travel/Locate has actually completed; it is the authoritative promotion point from pending target to current destination.

candidates.name: Existing React current/pending destination state
candidates.reason: A pendingDestinationId/mode pair around the existing request callback closes the semantic gap without new state-machine infrastructure.

candidates.name: Keep optimistic ACTIVE before native arrival
candidates.reason: Conflicts with aria-current=location semantics and leaves failed targets visually/currently misrepresented after a route interruption.

decision.rationale: Preserve one destination model and one YEIS camera authority. Product scenes remain immediate ACTIVE because the product render changes immediately; native travel/Locate requests carry destinationId and remain pending until the existing autopilot completion callback promotes them. Navigator renders pending mode separately and reserves aria-current=location for genuinely current destinations. Failure clears pending and never promotes the failed target.
decision.fallback: If future native travel needs rollback to a previous camera location, add previous-current restoration to the same request transaction; do not reintroduce optimistic ACTIVE.
